cube.title: Cube by Before Semicolon
cube.intro: A headless, themeable web-component library for visual editors. This prerelease implements media players, two chart families and shared foundations; the remaining design inventory is still in progress.
cube.guideBody: Import individual component entrypoints to register cb-* tags automatically. Headless base entrypoints do not register elements. The root package exposes DOM-free data utilities and loadComponent for lazy browser loading. Concrete HTMLElement classes require a DOM, including in Node or Deno.
cube.runtime: Browser scripts require the web-component runtime first. Charts also need the ECharts runtime, or a custom configureChartEngine loader. Media-only scripts do not load ECharts. The current npm release has not been replaced by this branch.
cube.themeBody: ThemeProvider accepts a site-builder ThemeDefinitionV1 document through theme or src. appearance accepts light, dark or system. CSS token names match site-builder; nested providers create explicit scopes. JSON theme files and CSS are generated into dist/themes.
cube.mediaApi: Both players accept src, mediaTitle, muted, autoplay, loop, preload, seekStep, playbackRate, locale and labels. Video also accepts poster and tracks. All props are optional; autoplay is off by default. Methods: play, pause, stop, seek, backward, forward, setVolume, setMuted and setRate. Video supports fullscreen where the browser permits it.
cube.chartApi: CartesianChart accepts series, xAxis, yAxis, inverted, stacking and zoomable. Series types include line, spline, area, areaspline, bar, column, scatter, bubble, errorbar, x-threshold and y-threshold. Use stable series IDs. A secondary value axis is selected by its ID. Null values remain gaps; invalid values emit cb-error rather than becoming invented data.
cube.pieApi: PieChart accepts a series containing named data segments, plus variant (pie or donut), innerTitle and innerDescription. Each segment has an id, name and value (or y). Zero-only datasets render an empty state. Negative and non-finite values are rejected gracefully. Percentages use the visible-data total.
cube.commonCharts: Both charts support heading, description, height, status, locale, labels and valueFormatter. visibleSeries or visibleSegments makes filtering controlled; otherwise visibility is managed internally. Reassign data props after edits. cb-select reports point selection, cb-visibility-change reports filters, cb-retry requests a retry and cb-error reports recoverable errors.
cube.accessBody: Controls use native buttons, ranges and selects with injectable translated labels. Charts provide keyboard point navigation, visible legend controls, persistent details and a data table. Reduced motion is respected. Authors must supply meaningful data names, captions and transcripts. Automated checks do not replace screen-reader and usability review.
cube.parts: Media styling parts: player, media, title, controls, play, stop, backward, forward, seek, time, volume, mute, rate, captions, fullscreen, status and transcript. Chart parts: chart, title, description, legend, legend-item, plot, graphic, navigator, details, data, table and table-cell. Use theme variables and ::part; do not target the chart engine’s private markup.
cube.audioBody: A simple audio transport with play/pause, stop, configurable seek steps, volume and playback speed. A missing source shows a safe empty state. Backward and forward seek within the current media; they are not playlist navigation.
cube.videoBody: The same transport for video, with a poster, optional caption tracks and feature-detected fullscreen. The native media node survives prop and playback updates, so controls do not restart playback.
cube.cartesianBody: A single component for common Cartesian visualizations, powered by Apache ECharts. The functional reference is Cloudscape’s Cartesian chart; this is not a React wrapper or a pixel-for-pixel copy.
cube.pieBody: One component for pie and donut views, with filtering, segment details and optional center content. ECharts is loaded only when a populated chart mounts.
cube.figma: Figma references for these four additions remain pending because the connected plan’s tool-call quota is exhausted. Storybook provides the runnable visual reference in this branch.
